For your office assistant duties you'll report to the Managing Director, providing practical administrative support that keeps the office running smoothly and helps the wider business operate efficiently. Working across both areas, you'll be a key point of contact for colleagues and gain broad exposure to how the business runs.

Key responsibilities

Finance (reporting to the Finance Director)

Sales Ledger & Credit Control
- Allocating customer receipts daily and reviewing and issuing sales invoices
- Processing card payments by telephone, pay-by-link and online
- Chasing overdue accounts by phone and email, and supporting the reduction of aged debt
- Resolving customer account queries and processing refunds

Purchase Ledger
- Collating and posting purchase invoices, ensuring payments stay within terms
- Matching invoices to purchase orders and resolving supplier queries
- Reconciling supplier statements and maintaining supplier records
- Preparing BACS runs and ad-hoc payments for approval

Banking & General Finance Support
- Accurately recording all cash movements and assisting with bank reconciliations
- Maintaining accurate accounting records and helping manage the finance inbox
- Supporting the Assistant Accountant and Finance Director with ad-hoc tasks

Office & Business Support (reporting to the Managing Director)

- Assisting with basic HR administration, including new starter paperwork and holiday records
- Managing incoming and outgoing post, couriers and deliveries
- Ordering and monitoring office supplies, stationery and consumables
- Diary management, arranging meetings and booking rooms, travel and accommodation as required
- Preparing letters, documents, spreadsheets and presentations
- Liaising with suppliers and contractors for office services such as cleaning, maintenance and IT
- Helping to keep the office environment tidy, organised and welcoming
- Supporting the Managing Director and colleagues across the business with general administrative tasks and projects

What you'll bring
- Sound experience in bookkeeping and financial administration, ideally combined with general office or administrative experience
- Strong attention to detail, with the ability to spot discrepancies and investigate issues
- Good Excel skills and confident use of Word and Outlook. Experience of an ERP level system is also advantageous
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a professional and friendly telephone manner
- The ability to manage a varied workload across different functions, balance priorities from more than one manager and work independently to deadlines
- A proactive, flexible and organised approach, with a willingness to get involved wherever help is needed

Benefits
- Quarterly bonus scheme
- 23 days' holiday plus bank holidays, with a holiday buyback scheme
- Study support towards AAT or other professional qualifications for the right candidate, if desired
- Company-funded Health Cash Plan
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Cycle-to-work scheme

This role is primarily office-based, with flexible and remote working arrangements available ad hoc.

title: Payroll Administrator
salary_text: £34000 - £36000 per year (Up to c£36k depending on expereince)
description:
Our client is a well-respected business with close to 2,000 employees. We are looking for an experienced Payroll Administrator who can work as part of a team to handle the business's payroll requirements.

This is a full-time permanent position and the hours are 8:30am-5:30pm Monday to Friday (40 hour working week).

Details of the position are as follows:

Person Specification

Essential
- Proven experience in payroll administration or a similar role.
- Strong knowledge of payroll processes, including statutory payments (SSP, SMP, SPP, etc.).
- Understanding of payroll year-end processes including P60s, P11 Ds, and P45s.
- Good understanding of UK PAYE, National Insurance, and HMRC reporting requirements.
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Ability to handle confidential information with discretion.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise and meet strict deadlines.
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team.

Desirable
- Experience using payroll software (e.g., iTrent, Sage, or similar).
- Experience working in a multi-site or large business environment.
- Knowledge of pension auto-enrolment processes.
- Experience liaising with HMRC and other third-party providers.
- Awareness of GDPR and data protection compliance within payroll.

Main Accountabilities and Responsibilities

Payroll Processing & Compliance
- Accurately process monthly payroll in line with company deadlines, ensuring compliance with HMRC and statutory requirements.
- Collate, review, and input data for new starters, leavers, overtime, expenses, bonuses, and other payroll exceptions.
- Submit payroll files to MHR and manage the validation process, resolving discrepancies before final submission.
- Prepare and submit BACS payments, PAYE, and payroll certificates, ensuring all approvals are in place.
- Maintain awareness of legislative changes impacting payroll and statutory payments.

Pensions & Benefits Administration
- Administer pension auto-enrolment, opt-ins, opt-outs, and re-enrolment cycles for all brands.
- Produce pension letters and upload to colleague records, ensuring regulatory compliance.
- Manage colleague benefit data (private health care, group income protection, life assurance) and liaise with providers on updates and renewals.
- Produce accurate reports to support gender pay gap submissions, P11 D reporting, and other statutory filings.

Reporting & Data Management
- Maintain accurate and confidential payroll and HR records to support audits and reporting requirements.
- Spot-check payroll monthly and provide findings to the HR Manager.
- Update and share bonus eligibility and absence reports with Finance and HR teams.
- Liaise with HMRC and other external agencies regarding tax codes, statutory payments, and compliance queries.

Colleague Support
- Act as the first point of contact for payroll and benefit queries, resolving issues promptly and professionally.
- Provide guidance to colleagues on statutory pay entitlements including maternity, paternity, and SSP.
